ko_bearing#0.title: 베어링
ko_bearing#0.text:
베어링(bearing, 문화어: 축받치개)은 원하는 움직임에 대한 상대 운동을 제한하고 움직이는 부분사이의 마찰을 줄여주는 기계요소(machine element)의 하나로, 회전이나 왕복 운동을 하는 축을 일정한 위치에서 지지하여 자유롭게 움직이게 하는 기계장치(부품)이다. 예를 들어, 베어링의 설계는 선형 가동부의 움직임과 고정 축을 중심으로 하는 회전을 자유롭게 제공한다. 또는 벡터의 수직력을 제한함으로써 움직임의 부담을 예방한다. 많은 베어링들은 또한 마찰을 최소화 시켜 가능한 많이 원하는 모션을 용이하게 한다. 베어링은 모션이 허락하는 작업의 종류나 적용하는 부분의 하중(힘)의 방향에 따라 크게 분류된다.
간단하게 베어링은 베어링 표면, 형태, 크기, 제어 할 다양한 각도, 부분으로 절단되거나 형성된 요철 면과의 위치이다. 다른 베어링은 기계 또는 기계 부분의 설치 별도의 장치이다. 가장 까다로운 애플리케이션을 위한 가장 섬세한 베어링은 매우 정확한 장비이다. 이와 같은 제조는 현존하는 기술 중 최고의 기술을 요구로 한다.
미끄럼 베어링인 배빗메탈, 구름 베어링인 볼 베어링, 롤러베어링 등이 있다.

축을 정확하고 매끄럽게 회전시키기 위해서 사용된다. 마찰에 의한 에너지 손실이나 발열을 줄여, 부품의 손상을 감소시킨다. 수송 기계부터 시작해서 각종 기계에 널리 사용되며, 회전하는 부분이 있는 기계장치에는 반드시 존재한다.
ko_bearing#0.en:
Bearings (bearing, technical term: shaft support) are one of the machine elements (machine components) that limit relative motion to desired movements and reduce friction between moving parts. Bearings support shafts undergoing rotation or reciprocating motion at fixed positions, allowing free movement. For example, bearing design provides free movement for linear actuators and rotational motion about a fixed shaft axis. Alternatively, it prevents movement load by limiting vertical vector forces. Many bearings also minimize friction to facilitate desired motion. Bearings are broadly classified according to the type of motion allowed and the direction of load (force) applied to the component.

Simply put, bearings are defined by bearing surfaces, shapes, sizes, controllable angles, and the position of formed or cut grooves on the surfaces. Other bearings are separate devices for installation on machines or machine components. The most precise bearings for the most demanding applications are extremely accurate equipment. Such manufacturing requires the highest level of technology available today.  

Sliding bearings such as ball bearings, rolling bearings such as roller bearings, and ball bearings exist.

They are used to rotate shafts accurately and smoothly. By reducing energy losses and heat generation due to friction, they minimize component damage. Bearings are widely used in various machines, from transportation equipment to all kinds of machinery, and are always present in any machine with rotating parts.

de_hydrodynamisches_gleitlager#4.title: Hydrodynamisches Gleitlager
de_hydrodynamisches_gleitlager#4.text:
Begrenzte Notlaufeigenschaften

Hydrostatische Gleitlager haben einen geringeren Leistungsbedarf (Pumpleistung plus Lagerreibung) als hydrodynamische, weil diese als Pumpen mit schlechtem Wirkungsgrad arbeiten. Das ändert sich bei hohen Umfangsgeschwindigkeiten, bei denen die Strömung in den Kammern der hydrostatischen Lager turbulent wird, so dass der günstigere Pump-Wirkungsgrad für den Leistungsbedarf nicht mehr entscheidend ist.
Hydrodynamische Lager werden aber auch bei nicht sehr hohen Drehzahlen aus Sicherheitsgründen bevorzugt, weil eine Ölversorgung von 50 bis 1000 bar ein Risiko darstellt. Dieses wird z. B. bei Turbinen trotz möglicher Leistungseinsparung nicht eingegangen. Eine zusätzliche Ölpumpe (< 50 bar) wird nur beim Auslaufen und Wiederanfahren eingeschaltet, was bei Turbinen selten auftritt.
Hydrostatische Gleitlager werden bevorzugt, wenn Wellen möglichst zentrisch laufen müssen (z. B. bei Werkzeugmaschinenspindeln), aber etwa 90 % aller Gleitlager laufen hydrodynamisch.

Das hydrodynamische Gleitlager kommt in vielen verschiedenen Anwendungen und Industrien zum Einsatz. Typische Anwendungen für Halbschalenlager und Gleitlagerbuchsen sind Motoren, Getriebe, Kompressoren und Pumpen sowie Lagerungen von Anlagen in zum Beispiel der metallverarbeitenden Industrie. Typische Einsatzgebiete für hydrodynamische Gleitlager sind Nutzfahrzeuge, Offhighway-Fahrzeuge, Schifffahrt, Luftfahrt, Energieerzeugung (Windkraft) sowie die verschiedensten industriellen Anwendungen.
de_hydrodynamisches_gleitlager#4.en:
Limited ability to operate at reduced speed

Hydrostatic journal bearings have a lower power requirement (pump power plus bearing friction) than hydrodynamic bearings, because the latter operate as pumps with poor efficiency. This changes at high peripheral speeds, where the flow in the chambers of hydrostatic bearings becomes turbulent, so that the advantageous pump efficiency is no longer decisive for the power requirement.  
Hydrodynamic bearings are nevertheless preferred even at not very high speeds for safety reasons, because an oil supply of 50 to 1000 bar represents a risk. This is for example not accepted in turbines despite possible power savings. An additional oil pump (< 50 bar) is only activated during startup and re-starting, which rarely occurs in turbines.  
Hydrostatic journal bearings are preferred when shafts must run as centrally as possible (e.g. in machine tool spindles), but approximately 90 % of all journal bearings operate hydrodynamically.

The hydrodynamic journal bearing is used in many different applications and industries. Typical applications for half-shield bearings and journal bearing sleeves are engines, transmissions, compressors and pumps, as well as mountings of equipment in for example the metalworking industry. Typical application areas for hydrodynamic journal bearings are commercial vehicles, off-highway vehicles, shipping, aviation, energy generation (wind power) as well as various industrial applications.

en_tapered_roller_bearing#2.title: Tapered roller bearing
en_tapered_roller_bearing#2.text:
These were called journal bearings and relied on the lubricant to form a fluid bearing. Without adequate lubrication, journal bearings would fail due to the excessive heat caused by friction. Timken was able to significantly reduce the friction on his axle bearings by adding tapered elements which actually rolled while transferring the load evenly from axle to frame through the hardened steel inner and outer rings and the rollers – his tapered roller bearing.
The tapered roller bearing in combination with modern lubricants is extremely durable and is used almost universally in applications involving rotating axle and transmission shafts. Bearing durability is such that these shafts often require no maintenance for hundreds of thousands of kilometers of operation.

In many applications tapered roller bearings are used in back-to-back pairs so that axial forces can be supported equally in either direction.
Pairs of tapered roller bearings are used in car and vehicle wheel bearings where they must cope simultaneously with large vertical (radial) and horizontal (axial) forces. Tapered roller bearings are commonly used for moderate speed, heavy duty applications where durability is required. Common real world applications are in agriculture, construction and mining equipment, sports robot combat, axle systems, gear box, engine motors and reducers, propeller shaft, railroad axle-box, differential, wind turbines, etc. A tapered roller bearing is a unit that consists of both tapered raceways (inner and outer rings), and tapered rollers. The construction is intended for combination loads, such as dual acting axial and radial loads.

ko_ball_bearing#1.title: 볼 베어링
ko_ball_bearing#1.text:
그의 설계는 차축 어셈블리의 홈을 따라 볼이 움직이는 최초의 현대적인 볼 베어링 설계이다.
파리의 자전거 정비사인 쥘 쉬리레는 1869년에 최초의 레이디얼 스타일 볼 베어링을 설계했으며 이는 1869년 11월 세계 최초의 자전거 도로 경주인 파리-루앙에서 제임스 무어가 타고 우승한 자전거에 장착되었다.

볼 베어링에는 여러 가지 일반적인 디자인이 있으며, 각 디자인은 다양한 성능 절충점을 제공한다. 이들은 스테인리스강, 크롬강, 세라믹 (질화 규소, Si3N4)을 포함한 다양한 재료로 만들어질 수 있다. 하이브리드 볼 베어링은 세라믹 볼과 금속 레이스를 가진 베어링이다.

앵귤러 콘택트 볼 베어링은 축 방향으로 비대칭인 레이스를 사용한다. 축 방향 하중은 베어링을 통해 직선으로 전달되는 반면, 반경 방향 하중은 레이스를 축 방향으로 분리시키는 경사 경로를 따른다. 따라서 내륜의 접촉각은 외륜의 접촉각과 동일하다. 앵귤러 콘택트 베어링은 복합 하중(반경 방향 및 축 방향 모두의 하중)을 더 잘 지지하며, 베어링의 접촉각은 각 하중의 상대적 비율에 맞춰야 한다. 접촉각이 클수록(일반적으로 10~45도 범위) 지지되는 축 하중은 높지만 반경 하중은 낮아진다.
ko_ball_bearing#1.en:
His design was the first modern rolling bearing design in which the balls move along the housing of the axle assembly.  
The bicycle mechanic Chu Shiryé designed the first radial-style rolling bearing in 1869, and it was fitted to the bicycle ridden by James Moore, who won the world's first bicycle road race, the Paris–Lyon race, in November 1869.

Rolling bearings have several common designs, each providing different performance trade-offs. They can be manufactured from various materials, including stainless steel, chrome steel, and ceramics (silicon nitride, Si3N4). Hybrid rolling bearings are bearings with ceramic balls and metallic races.

Angular contact rolling bearings use asymmetric races along the axis. Axial loads are transmitted straight through the bearing, while radial loads follow a slanted path that separates the races along the axis. Therefore, the contact angle of the inner ring is equal to that of the outer ring. Angular contact bearings support combined loads (radial and axial) better, and the bearing's contact angle must match the relative proportions of each load. The larger the contact angle (typically in the range of 10–45 degrees), the higher the axial load capacity, but the radial load capacity decreases.

ko_bearing#3.title: 베어링
ko_bearing#3.text:
접촉부분이 면이므로 상대적으로 큰 하중을 지지할 수 있다. 자동차의 크랭크 축에 쓰이게 되는데 이물질에 취약하다.
유체베어링(fluid bearing) - 금속간에 유체가 존재하여 금속간 마찰이 없어 소음이 적고 수명이 길지만 저온에서 정상작동을 보장하기 힘들고, 기름이 유출되면 더 이상 회전이 불가능하고, 중력 현상으로 인한 금속마찰이 있을 수 있다. 회전체의 한 점이 회전중심으로부터 안정적으로 돌 수 있어, 정밀도와 장수명을 요구하는 하드디스크 모터나 저소음을 요구하는 쿨링팬에 쓰인다.
자기베어링 (magnetic bearing) - 자기부상을 이용하는 베어링으로, 이론상으로는 마찰이 전혀 없어야 하나, 실제로는 보조 베어링이 같이 쓰인다. 가장 낮은 소음이 기대되는 방식으로 발전소 등의 대형 모터에서 주로 쓰여 왔으나, 최근에 컴퓨터 케이스 팬에도 이 방식울 채택한 제품이 출시됨. 10 dB대의 가장 낮은 수준의 소음과 고속 회전이 가능하며, 가장 높은 내구성을 갖추었다고 알려져 있다.
슬리브베어링 (sleeve bearing) - 볼베어링 방식에 비해 낮은 소음이 장점이나, 비교적 낮은 내구성(내열성 및 수명)이 단점이다. 높은 회전속도에서는 고발열로 인해 수명이 급격하게 단축되므로 높은 회전 속도와 내구성을 요구하지 않는 케이스 팬으로 채용된다.
ko_bearing#3.en:
The contact surface is a plane, thus capable of supporting relatively large loads. It is used in automobile crankshafts, but is susceptible to contaminants.

Fluid bearing (fluid bearing) - A bearing where a fluid exists between metal surfaces, eliminating metal-to-metal friction, resulting in low noise and long life. However, it is difficult to ensure normal operation at low temperatures, and rotation becomes impossible if oil leaks out. Metal friction due to gravity may also occur. Because one point of the rotating element can rotate stably around the center, it is used in hard disk motors requiring high precision and longevity, and in cooling fans requiring low noise.

Magnetic bearing (magnetic bearing) - A bearing utilizing magnetic levitation. Theoretically, it should have absolutely no friction, but in practice, auxiliary bearings are used. It has been primarily used in large motors such as those in power plants, where the lowest noise levels are expected. Recently, products adopting this method have also been launched in computer case fans. It is known to achieve the lowest noise level in the 10 dB range, allow high-speed rotation, and offer the highest durability.

Sleeve bearing (sleeve bearing) - It has the advantage of lower noise compared to ball bearings, but has relatively low durability (thermal resistance and lifespan). At high rotational speeds, it suffers rapid lifespan reduction due to excessive heat generation. Therefore, it is used in case fans where high rotational speed and durability are not required.

ko_ball_bearing#8.title: 볼 베어링
ko_ball_bearing#8.text:
스냅 링은 플랜지 기능을 담당한다.
케이지형
케이지는 일반적으로 콘래드 스타일 볼 베어링에서 볼을 고정하는 데 사용된다. 다른 구조 유형에서는 특정 케이지 모양에 따라 볼의 수가 줄어들어 하중 지지력이 감소할 수 있다. 케이지가 없으면 접선 위치는 두 개의 볼록한 표면이 서로 미끄러지면서 안정화된다. 케이지가 있으면 접선 위치는 볼록한 표면이 일치하는 오목한 표면에서 미끄러지면서 안정화되는데, 이는 볼에 흠집이 생기는 것을 방지하고 마찰이 적다. 케이지형 롤러 베어링은 존 해리슨이 18세기 중반 크로노그래프 작업의 일환으로 발명했다.
세라믹 볼을 사용한 하이브리드 볼 베어링
세라믹 베어링 볼은 크기와 재료에 따라 강철 볼보다 최대 40% 가볍다. 이는 원심 하중과 미끄러짐을 줄여주므로 하이브리드 세라믹 베어링은 기존 베어링보다 20%에서 40% 더 빠르게 작동할 수 있다. 이는 베어링이 회전할 때 외륜 홈이 볼에 가하는 안쪽 방향 힘이 줄어든다는 것을 의미한다. 이러한 힘의 감소는 마찰과 마찰력#구름 마찰력을 줄인다. 가벼운 볼은 베어링을 더 빠르게 회전시키고, 속도를 유지하는 데 더 적은 전력을 사용한다. 세라믹 볼은 일반적으로 레이스보다 단단하다. 마모로 인해 시간이 지남에 따라 레이스에 홈이 생길 것이다.
ko_ball_bearing#8.en:
Snap ring performs the flange function.  
Cage-type  
The cage is generally used to hold balls in a concord style ball bearing. In other structural types, the number of balls may decrease depending on the specific cage shape, which can reduce load-carrying capacity. Without a cage, the tangential position is stabilized by two convex surfaces sliding against each other. With a cage, the tangential position is stabilized by sliding between concave surfaces that match the convex surfaces, which prevents scratches on the balls and reduces friction. Cage-type roller bearings were invented by John Harrison in the mid-18th century as part of chronograph work.  
Hybrid ball bearing using ceramic balls  
Ceramic bearing balls are up to 40% lighter than steel balls in size and material. This reduces centrifugal load and sliding, allowing hybrid ceramic bearings to operate 20% to 40% faster than conventional bearings. This means that the inward force applied by the outer raceway housing to the balls during rotation is reduced. This reduction in force decreases friction and ceramic friction. Lighter balls enable faster rotation of the bearing and require less power to maintain speed. Ceramic balls are generally harder than races. Over time due to wear, holes will form in the races.

ko_bearing#2.title: 베어링
ko_bearing#2.text:
캡쳐 또는 갇힌 볼 베어링은 원래 갈릴레오가 17세기에 고안했다.
최초의 실용적인 갇힌 롤러 베어링은 1740년대 중반에 시계학자 존 해리슨이 발명하였다. 이는 매우 제한된 운동을 위한 베어링이지만 해리슨은 현대에 존재하는 일반 시계의 회전 애플리케이션과 유사한 베어링을 사용하였다.

구름베어링(rolling bearing)
볼베어링(ball bearing) - 슬리브 방식에 비해 높은 내구성(내열성 및 수명)이 장점이나, 시끄로운 소음이 단점. 내구성이 높고, 고속의 회전을 견딜 수 있어서 중앙처리장치 냉각장치, 하드디스크 모터, 시디롬 모터 등에 적용된다. 볼의 형태에 따라 2볼 베어링 등 다양하게 불린다.
롤러베어링(roller bearing) - 볼베어링의 볼이 들어가는 부분에 원통 모양의 롤러가 들어간다.내구성이 좋고 큰 중량도 잘 버티므로 자동차의 휠에 들어간다.
플레인베어링(plain bearing) - 평평하고 넓은 면으로 축을 지지한다. 접촉부분이 면이므로 상대적으로 큰 하중을 지지할 수 있다. 자동차의 크랭크 축에 쓰이게 되는데 이물질에 취약하다.
ko_bearing#2.en:
Caged or captive ball bearing was originally conceived by Galileo in the 17th century.  
The first practical caged rolling bearing was invented by clockmaker John Harrison in the mid-1740s. Although this bearing allows only very limited motion, Harrison used a bearing similar to those found in modern clocks for rotational applications.

Rolling bearing  
Ball bearing – Advantages over sleeve type include higher durability (thermal resistance and lifespan), but disadvantage is noisy operation. High durability and ability to withstand high-speed rotation make it applicable in central processing unit cooling devices, hard disk motors, CD-ROM motors, etc. It is referred to by various names depending on the shape of the balls, such as double ball bearing.  
Roller bearing – Cylindrical rollers are inserted into the portion where balls would normally be placed in a ball bearing. It has good durability and can withstand heavy loads, thus it is used in automobile wheels.  
Plain bearing – Supports the shaft with a flat and wide surface. Since the contact area is a surface, it can support relatively large loads. It is used in automobile crankshafts, but is susceptible to contamination.

en_rolling_element_bearing#2.title: Rolling-element bearing
en_rolling_element_bearing#2.text:
17th century - Galileo describes the functionality of a caged bearing
1740 - John Harrison invented the first caged roller bearing for H3 marine timekeeping.
1794 - The first patent for the ball race was given to Philip Vaughan of Carmarthen, Wales. This is the first design seen with a spherical object moving through a groove.
1869 - Jules Suriray receives the first patent for a radial ball bearing, his design was used by James Moore to win the first 80 mi (130 km) bicycle race from Paris to Rouen.

Design description
Bearings, especially rolling element bearings, are designed in a similar fashion across the board consisting of the outer and inner track, a central bore, a retainer to keep the rolling elements from clashing into one another or seizing the bearing movement, and the rolling elements themselves.
The internal rolling components may differ in design due to their intended purpose of application of the bearing. The main five types of bearings are ball, cylindrical, tapered, barrel, and needle.
Ball - the simplest following the basic principles with minimal design intention. Important to note the ability for more seizures is likely due to the freedom of the track design.
Cylindrical - For single axis movement for straight directional movement. The shape allows for more surface area to be in contact adding in moving more weight with less force at a greater distance.
Tapered - Primarily focused on the ability to take on axial loading and radial loading. It does this by using a conical structure enabling the elements to roll diagonally.

ko_ball_bearing#0.title: 볼 베어링
ko_ball_bearing#0.text:
볼 베어링(ball bearing)은 베어링의 레이스 사이의 간격을 유지하기 위해 볼을 사용하는 구름 베어링의 일종이다.
볼 베어링의 목적은 회전 마찰력을 줄이고 반경 및 축 하중을 지지하는 것이다. 이는 최소 두 개의 레이스를 사용하여 볼을 수용하고 볼을 통해 하중을 전달함으로써 달성된다. 대부분의 응용 분야에서 한 레이스는 고정되어 있고 다른 레이스는 회전 어셈블리(예: 허브 또는 샤프트)에 부착된다. 베어링 레이스 중 하나가 회전하면 볼도 회전하게 된다. 볼이 구르기 때문에 두 평평한 표면이 서로 미끄러지는 것보다 마찰 계수가 훨씬 낮다.
볼 베어링은 볼과 레이스 사이의 접촉 면적이 작기 때문에 다른 종류의 구름 베어링보다 크기에 비해 하중 지지력이 낮은 경향이 있다. 그러나 내륜과 외륜의 약간의 어긋남은 허용할 수 있다.
일반적인 볼 베어링 설계에는 앵귤러 콘택트, 축방향, 딥 그루브 및 사전 장착된 쌍이 포함된다. 볼 베어링의 볼은 다양한 방식으로 구성될 수도 있다. 볼 베어링은 스케이트보드 (장비) 및 원심펌프를 포함한 광범위한 응용 분야에 사용된다.

베어링은 고대부터 개발되었지만, 볼 베어링에 대한 최초의 현대적인 기록 특허는 1794년 카마던에서 볼 베어링의 첫 설계를 만든 웨일스 발명가이자 제철업자인 필립 본에게 수여되었다.
ko_ball_bearing#0.en:
Ball bearing (ball bearing) is a type of rolling bearing that uses balls to maintain the gap between the bearing races.  
The purpose of a ball bearing is to reduce rotational friction and support radial and axial loads. This is achieved by using at least two races to accommodate the balls and transferring the load through the balls. In most applications, one race is fixed and the other is attached to a rotating assembly (e.g., hub or shaft). When one of the bearing races rotates, the balls also rotate. Since the balls roll, the coefficient of friction is much lower than when two flat surfaces slide against each other.  
Ball bearings tend to have lower load-carrying capacity relative to their size because the contact area between the balls and the races is small. However, a slight misalignment between the inner and outer rings is acceptable.  
Common ball bearing designs include angular contact, thrust, deep groove, and pre-assembled pairs. The balls in a ball bearing can be configured in various ways. Ball bearings are used in a wide range of applications, including skateboards (equipment) and centrifugal pumps.  

Bearings have been developed since ancient times, but the first modern patent related to ball bearings was granted in 1794 to Philip Bon, a Welsh inventor and ironmaster, who designed the first ball bearing in Calamond.

en_ball_bearing#7.title: Ball bearing
en_ball_bearing#7.text:
The snap ring assumes the function of a flange.
Caged
Cages are typically used to secure the balls in a Conrad-style ball bearing. In other construction types they may decrease the number of balls depending on the specific cage shape, and thus reduce the load capacity. Without cages the tangential position is stabilized by sliding of two convex surfaces on each other. With a cage the tangential position is stabilized by a sliding of a convex surface in a matched concave surface, which avoids dents in the balls and has lower friction. Caged roller bearings were invented by John Harrison in the mid-18th century as part of his work on chronographs.
Hybrid ball bearings using ceramic balls
Ceramic bearing balls can weigh up to 40% less than steel ones, depending on size and material. This reduces centrifugal loading and skidding, so hybrid ceramic bearings can operate 20% to 40% faster than conventional bearings. This means that the outer race groove exerts less force inward against the ball as the bearing spins. This reduction in force reduces the friction and rolling resistance. The lighter balls allow the bearing to spin faster, and uses less power to maintain its speed. The ceramic balls are typically harder than the race. Due to wear, with time they will form a groove in the race. This is preferable to the balls wearing which would leave them with possible flat spots significantly harming performance. While ceramic hybrid bearings use ceramic balls in place of steel ones, they are constructed with steel inner and outer rings; hence the hybrid designation.

en_bearing_mechanical#1.title: Bearing (mechanical)
en_bearing_mechanical#1.text:
Lubricants come in different forms, including liquids, solids, and gases. The choice of lubricant depends on the specific application and factors such as temperature, load, and speed. In the ball bearing and roller bearing, to reduce sliding friction, rolling elements such as rollers or balls with a circular cross-section are located between the races or journals of the bearing assembly. A wide variety of bearing designs exists to allow the demands of the application to be correctly met for maximum efficiency, reliability, durability, and performance.

It is sometimes assumed that the invention of the rolling bearing, in the form of wooden rollers supporting– or bearing –an object being moved, predates the invention of a wheel rotating on a plain bearing; this underlies speculation that cultures such as the Ancient Egyptians used roller bearings in the form of tree trunks under sleds. There is no archaeological evidence for this sequence of technological development. The Egyptian drawings in the tomb of Djehutihotep are believed to show the process of moving massive stone blocks not with rollers but upon sledges pulled over sand which was wetted to increase its cohesion and reduce friction. There are also Egyptian drawings of plain bearings used to support the far end of hand drills.
Wheeled vehicles using plain bearings emerged between about 5000 BC and 3000 BC.
A recovered example of an early rolling-element bearing is a wooden ball bearing supporting a rotating table from the remains of the Roman Nemi ships in Lake Nemi, Italy. The wrecks were dated to 40 BC.

de_gleitlager#1.title: Gleitlager
de_gleitlager#1.text:
Beim Anlauf der Welle entsteht zunächst Mischreibung. Mit zunehmender Drehzahl wird der Schmierstoff durch die Bewegung der Welle in den Spalt zwischen Welle und Lagerbuchse gezogen. Die Geometrie des Lagers ist oft so gestaltet, dass sie an einer Seite enger ist. Dies führt dazu, dass der Schmierstoff komprimiert wird und einen Druckaufbau erfährt. Der Druck im Schmierstoff hebt die Welle an und trennt sie von der Lagerbuchse, wodurch ein tragender Schmierfilm entsteht und die Welle auf dem Schmierfilm „schwimmt“.

Heute werden auch hydrodynamische Gleitlager mit spiralförmiger Nutung (engl. spiral groove bearing) eingesetzt, bei welchen das Schmiermittel bei rotierender Welle durch die Nut von außen zugeführt und ins Zentrum des Lagers befördert wird (Spiralrillenlager). Flach geätzte oder mit dem Laser herausgearbeitete Nuten sind häufig ausreichend. Eingesetzt wird die spiralförmige Nutung etwa bei besonders leise laufenden Computerlüftern. Schnelllaufende Lager bzw. dort, wo kein Flüssigkeiten eingesetzt werden dürfen, werden auch in luftgeschmierter Ausführung angeboten.
Ein hydrostatisches Gleitlager nutzt unter Druck zugeführtes Fluid (etwa durch eine Ölpumpe), um einen Schmierfilm zwischen den Lagerflächen zu erzeugen. Der Schmierfilm verhindert den Kontakt zwischen bewegten Elementen und den Lagerflächen und ermöglicht idealerweise eine nahezu reibungsfreie Bewegung. Im Gegensatz zum hydrodynamischen Gleitlager, bei dem der Schmierfilm durch die Relativbewegung der Welle selbst erzeugt wird, ist das hydrostatische Lager unabhängig von Bewegung und Belastung des Lagers.
de_gleitlager#1.en:
At startup of the shaft, initial mixed friction occurs. With increasing rotational speed, the lubricant is drawn into the gap between shaft and bearing bore by the motion of the shaft. The geometry of the bearing is often designed so that it is narrower on one side. This causes the lubricant to be compressed and a pressure build-up to occur. The pressure in the lubricant lifts the shaft and separates it from the bearing bore, thereby forming a load-carrying lubrication film and allowing the shaft to "float" on the lubrication film.

Today, hydrodynamic journal bearings with spiral grooves (English: spiral groove bearing) are also used, in which the lubricant is supplied from outside through the groove and conveyed to the center of the bearing (spiral groove bearing). Flat etched or laser-machined grooves are often sufficient. Spiral grooves are typically used in particularly quiet computer fans. High-speed bearings or those where liquids cannot be used are also available in air-lubricated versions.
A hydrostatic journal bearing uses pressurized fluid (e.g. supplied by an oil pump) to generate a lubrication film between the bearing surfaces. The lubrication film prevents contact between moving elements and bearing surfaces and enables ideally nearly frictionless motion. Unlike a hydrodynamic journal bearing, in which the lubrication film is generated by the relative motion of the shaft itself, the hydrostatic bearing is independent of bearing motion and load.

en_bearing_mechanical#2.title: Bearing (mechanical)
en_bearing_mechanical#2.text:
The wrecks were dated to 40 BC.
Leonardo da Vinci incorporated drawings of ball bearings in his design for a helicopter around the year 1500; this is the first recorded use of bearings in an aerospace design. However, Agostino Ramelli is the first to have published roller and thrust bearings sketches. An issue with the ball and roller bearings is that the balls or rollers rub against each other, causing additional friction. This can be reduced by enclosing each individual ball or roller within a cage. The captured, or caged, ball bearing was originally described by Galileo in the 17th century.
The first practical caged-roller bearing was invented in the mid-1740s by horologist John Harrison for his H3 marine timekeeper. In this timepiece, the caged bearing was only used for a very limited oscillating motion, but later on, Harrison applied a similar bearing design with a true rotational movement in a contemporaneous regulator clock.
The first patent on ball bearings was awarded to Philip Vaughan, a Welsh inventor and ironmaster in Carmarthen in 1794. His was the first modern ball-bearing design, with the ball running along a groove in the axle assembly.
Bearings played a pivotal role in the nascent Industrial Revolution, allowing the new industrial machinery to operate efficiently. For example, they were used for holding wheel and axle assemblies to greatly reduce friction compared to prior non-bearing designs.

The first patent for a radial-style ball bearing was awarded to Jules Suriray, a Parisian bicycle mechanic, on 3 August 1869.

de_lager_maschinenelement#3.text:

Im Gleitlager können die beiden sich gegeneinander bewegenden Teile gegebenenfalls in direktem Kontakt stehen. Sie gleiten gegen den durch Gleitreibung verursachten Widerstand. Dieser kann niedrig gehalten werden durch Wahl einer reibungsarmen Materialpaarung, durch Schmierung oder durch Erzeugen eines Schmierfilms, der die beiden Kontaktflächen voneinander trennt. Je nach Art der Schmierung unterscheidet man zwischen ungeschmierten bzw. selbstschmierenden Gleitlagern, hydrodynamischen Gleitlagern und hydrostatischen Gleitlagern. Als trennender Film kommt neben Flüssigkeiten (meistens Öl, seltener Wasser) auch Luft (Luftlager) vor.
Wenn sich die beiden Teile berühren, was bei ungeschmierten bzw. selbstschmierenden Gleitlagern der Fall ist, entsteht in den Kontaktflächen Verschleiß, der gegebenenfalls die Lebensdauer begrenzen kann.

Hingegen bei hydrodynamischen Gleitlagern schwimmt der Gegenlaufpartner auf dem Schmierfilm, was die Reibung auf ein Minimum reduziert und eine nahezu reibungsfreie Bewegung ermöglicht.
de_lager_maschinenelement#3.en:
A linear bearing is used to guide a straight-line motion between two bodies. The number of degrees of freedom is

f = 1.

It is the only bearing whose name clearly indicates what it allows (not what it prevents).
Sliding and rolling linear ball bearings are sleeve bearings guided on round shafts with

f = 2,

thus two of them are mounted parallel to each other to prevent rotational freedom.

In a sliding bearing, the two mutually moving parts may come into direct contact. They slide against the resistance caused by sliding friction. This resistance can be reduced by selecting a low-friction material pair, by lubrication, or by generating a lubrication film that separates the two contacting surfaces. Depending on the type of lubrication, sliding bearings are classified into unlubricated or self-lubricating bearings, hydrodynamic sliding bearings, and hydrostatic sliding bearings. In addition to liquids (usually oil, rarely water), air (air bearings) can serve as the separating film.

When the two parts come into contact, which occurs in unlubricated or self-lubricating sliding bearings, wear occurs at the contact surfaces, which may limit the service life.

In contrast, in hydrodynamic sliding bearings, the opposing member floats on the lubrication film, reducing friction to a minimum and enabling nearly frictionless motion.

en_rolling_element_bearing#1.title: Rolling-element bearing
en_rolling_element_bearing#1.text:
Rolling-element bearings have the advantage of a good trade-off between cost, size, weight, carrying capacity, durability, accuracy, friction, and so on. Other bearing designs are often better on one specific attribute, but worse in most other attributes, although fluid bearings can sometimes simultaneously outperform on carrying capacity, durability, accuracy, friction, rotation rate and sometimes cost. Only plain bearings are used as widely as rolling-element bearings. They are commonly used in automotive, industrial, marine, and aerospace applications. They are products of great necessity for modern technology. The rolling element bearing was developed from a firm foundation that was built over thousands of years. The concept emerged in its primitive form in Roman times. After a long inactive period in the Middle Ages, it was revived during the Renaissance by Leonardo da Vinci, and developed steadily in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

Beginning in 2600 BCE - The Ancient Egyptians were the first to notably use the concept behind rolling bearings, they first did this by using logs under these stones with groups of builders on either side to push and pull the weight of the stones.
40 BC - In the remains of a sunken Roman Ship in Lake Nemi. This discovery shows the continual development of the principle. The remains of the ship do not show clear signs of an indication of what these bearings were used for.
17th century - Galileo describes the functionality of a caged bearing
1740 - John Harrison invented the first caged roller bearing for H3 marine timekeeping.

en_fatigue_material#6.title: Fatigue (material)
en_fatigue_material#6.text:
1837: Wilhelm Albert publishes the first article on fatigue. He devised a test machine for conveyor chains used in the Clausthal mines.
1839: Jean-Victor Poncelet describes metals as being 'tired' in his lectures at the military school at Metz.
1842: William John Macquorn Rankine recognises the importance of stress concentrations in his investigation of railroad axle failures. The Versailles rail accident was caused by fatigue failure of a locomotive axle.
1843: Joseph Glynn reports on the fatigue of an axle on a locomotive tender. He identifies the keyway as the crack origin.
1848: The Railway Inspectorate reports one of the first tyre failures, probably from a rivet hole in tread of railway carriage wheel. It was likely a fatigue failure.
1849: Eaton Hodgkinson is granted a "small sum of money" to report to the UK Parliament on his work in "ascertaining by direct experiment, the effects of continued changes of load upon iron structures and to what extent they could be loaded without danger to their ultimate security".
1854: F. Braithwaite reports on common service fatigue failures and coins the term fatigue.
1860: Systematic fatigue testing undertaken by Sir William Fairbairn and August Wöhler.
1870: A. Wöhler summarises his work on railroad axles. He concludes that cyclic stress range is more important than peak stress and introduces the concept of endurance limit.
1903: Sir James Alfred Ewing demonstrates the origin of fatigue failure in microscopic cracks.
1910: O. H.

en_plain_bearing#1.title: Plain bearing
en_plain_bearing#1.text:
Axlebox bearings today are rolling-element bearings rather than plain bearings.
Linear bearing: This bearing provides linear motion; it may take the form of a circular bearing and shaft or any other two mating surfaces (e.g., a slide plate).
Thrust bearing: A thrust bearing provides a bearing surface for forces acting axial to the shaft. One example is a propeller shaft.

An integral plain bearing is built into the object of use as a hole prepared in the bearing surface. Industrial integral bearings are usually made from cast iron or babbitt, and a hardened steel shaft is used in the bearing.
Integral bearings are not as common because bushings are easier to accommodate and can be replaced if necessary. Depending on the material, an integral bearing may be less expensive but it cannot be replaced. If an integral bearing wears out, the item may be replaced or reworked to accept a bushing. Integral bearings were very common in 19th-century machinery but became progressively less common as interchangeable manufacture became popular.
For example, a common integral plain bearing is the door hinge, which is both a thrust bearing and a journal bearing.

A bushing, also known as a bush, is an independent plain bearing that is inserted into a housing to provide a bearing surface for rotary applications; this is the most common form of a plain bearing. Common designs include solid (sleeve and flanged), split, and clenched bushings.

en_plain_bearing#0.title: Plain bearing
en_plain_bearing#0.text:
A plain bearing, or more commonly sliding contact bearing and slide bearing (in railroading sometimes called a solid bearing, journal bearing, or friction bearing), is the simplest type of bearing, comprising only a bearing surface and no rolling elements. Therefore, the part of the shaft in contact with the bearing slides over the bearing surface. The simplest example of a plain bearing is a shaft rotating in a hole. A simple linear bearing can be a pair of flat surfaces designed to allow motion; e.g., a drawer and the slides it rests on or the ways on the bed of a lathe.
Plain bearings, in general, are the least expensive type of bearing. They are also compact and lightweight, and they have a high load-carrying capacity.

The design of a plain bearing depends on the type of motion the bearing must provide. The three types of motions possible are:

Journal (friction, radial or rotary) bearing: This is the most common type of plain bearing; it is simply a shaft rotating in a hole. It is also referred to as a sleeve bearing, especially in applications where a cylindrical bushing supports the shaft. In locomotive and railroad car applications journal bearing specifically referred to the plain bearings once used at the ends of the axles of railroad wheel sets, enclosed by axleboxes (also called journal boxes). Axlebox bearings today are rolling-element bearings rather than plain bearings.

en_tapered_roller_bearing#1.title: Tapered roller bearing
en_tapered_roller_bearing#1.text:
The non-separable cone assembly consists of the inner ring, the rollers, and a cage that retains and evenly spaces the rollers. The cup is simply the outer ring. Internal clearance is established during mounting by the axial position of the cone relative to the cup, although preloaded installations without clearance are common.
Metric tapered roller bearings follow the designation system defined by ISO 355.

On March 23, 1895, John Lincoln Scott, a farmer and carpenter from Wilmot, Indiana applied for a patent from the United States Patent Office for his invention of a roller bearing that fit on "the axle-skeins and hubs of wagons, buggies, or other wheeled vehicles". The bearing was composed of two sets of cylindrical rollers, one set larger in diameter than the other, that fit on flats machined on the tapered axle-skein. In 1898, Henry Timken was awarded a patent for the tapered roller bearing which used conical rollers. At the time, Timken was a carriage-maker in St. Louis and held three patents for carriage springs. However, it was his patent for tapered roller bearings that allowed his company to become successful.
Tapered roller bearings were a breakthrough at the end of the 19th century because bearings used in wheel axles had not changed much since ancient times. They consisted of a cylindrical seat on the frame and part of the axle enclosed in a case or box that held a lubricant. These were called journal bearings and relied on the lubricant to form a fluid bearing.

en_bearing_mechanical#3.title: Bearing (mechanical)
en_bearing_mechanical#3.text:
The first patent for a radial-style ball bearing was awarded to Jules Suriray, a Parisian bicycle mechanic, on 3 August 1869. The bearings were then fitted to the winning bicycle ridden by James Moore in the world's first bicycle road race, Paris-Rouen, in November 1869.
In 1883, Friedrich Fischer, founder of FAG, developed an approach for milling and grinding balls of equal size and exact roundness by means of a suitable production machine, which set the stage for the creation of an independent bearing industry. His hometown Schweinfurt later became a world-leading center for ball bearing production.

The modern, self-aligning design of ball bearing is attributed to Sven Wingquist of the SKF ball-bearing manufacturer in 1907 when he was awarded Swedish patent No. 25406 on its design.
Henry Timken, a 19th-century visionary and innovator in carriage manufacturing, patented the tapered roller bearing in 1898. The following year he formed a company to produce his innovation. Over a century, the company grew to make bearings of all types, including specialty steel bearings and an array of related products and services.
Erich Franke invented and patented the wire race bearing in 1934. His focus was on a bearing design with a cross-section as small as possible and which could be integrated into the enclosing design. After World War II, he founded with Gerhard Heydrich the company Franke & Heydrich KG (today Franke GmbH) to push the development and production of wire race bearings.

en_tribology#2.title: Tribology
en_tribology#2.text:
Other pioneers of tribology research are Australian physicist Frank Philip Bowden and British physicist David Tabor, both of the Cavendish Laboratory at Cambridge University. Together they wrote the seminal textbook The Friction and Lubrication of Solids (Part I originally published in 1950 and Part II in 1964). Michael J. Neale was another leader in the field during the mid-to-late 1900s. He specialized in solving problems in machine design by applying his knowledge of tribology. Neale was respected as an educator with a gift for integrating theoretical work with his own practical experience to produce easy-to-understand design guides. The Tribology Handbook, which he first edited in 1973 and updated in 1995, is still used around the world and forms the basis of numerous training courses for engineering designers.
Duncan Dowson surveyed the history of tribology in his 1997 book History of Tribology (2nd edition). This covers developments from prehistory, through early civilizations (Mesopotamia, ancient Egypt) and highlights the key developments up to the end of the twentieth century.

The term tribology became widely used following The Jost Report published in 1966. The report highlighted the huge cost of friction, wear and corrosion to the UK economy (1.1–1.4% of GDP). As a result, the UK government established several national centres to address tribological problems. Since then the term has diffused into the international community, with many specialists now identifying as "tribologists".

Despite considerable research since the Jost Report, the global impact of friction and wear on energy consumption, economic expenditure, and carbon dioxide emissions are still considerable.

de_waelzlager#2.title: Wälzlager
de_waelzlager#2.text:
Fischer und Wilhelm Höpflinger entwickelten die Kugelschleifmaschine entscheidend weiter. Nun konnten Kugeln mit sehr geringer Abweichung von der Idealform produziert werden. Diese Idee gilt als historischer Beginn der Wälzlagerindustrie.
1890–1910: Kugellagerpatente von den Schweinfurter Industriellen Friedrich Fischer, Wilhelm Höpflinger, Ernst Sachs sowie von August Riebe
1898 meldete Henry Timken in den USA ein Patent für das Kegelrollenlager an. Heute Timken Company.
1898–1901: Die Grundlagen der Wälzkörpertechnik wurden von der Technischen Versuchsanstalt Potsdam-Neubabelsberg unter der Leitung von Richard Stribeck erstmals wissenschaftlich untersucht.
1907: Sven Gustaf Wingqvist erfand das Pendelkugellager und gründete in Göteborg die Firma Svenska Kullagerfabriken – SKF.
1934: Erich Franke erfand das Drahtwälzlager nach dem Prinzip der eingelegten Laufdrähte.
Im Laufe der Zeit kamen zahlreiche weitere Varianten hinzu. Insbesondere entwickelten sich die Fertigungsgenauigkeit und die Schmierstoffentwicklung weiter. Zahlreiche Normen legten auch gängige Standardabmessungen fest und vereinfachten so Konstruktion und Fertigung. Heute werden Lager mit integrierten Sensoren wie elektronischer Kraft- und Verschleißermittlung angeboten.

1883 baute Friedrich Fischer in Schweinfurt die erste Kugelschleifmaschine und legte damit den Grundstein für die industrielle Fertigung von runden Stahlkugeln hinreichender Genauigkeit und der Wälzlagerindustrie. Im selben Jahr gründete er die Firma Kugelfischer. Sein Mitarbeiter Wilhelm Höpflinger entwickelte die Kugelschleifmaschine entscheidend weiter.
de_waelzlager#2.en:
Fischer and Wilhelm Höpflinger significantly advanced the ball grinding machine. Now balls with very small deviations from ideal shape could be produced. This idea is considered the historical starting point of the rolling bearing industry.  
1890–1910: Ball bearing patents by the Schweinfurter industrialists Friedrich Fischer, Wilhelm Höpflinger, Ernst Sachs, and August Riebe  
1898 Henry Timken filed a patent in the USA for the conical roller bearing. Today Timken Company.  
1898–1901: The fundamentals of rolling element technology were first scientifically investigated by the Technical Research Institute Potsdam-Neubabelsberg under the leadership of Richard Stribeck.  
1907: Sven Gustaf Wingqvist invented the pendulum ball bearing and founded in Gothenburg the company Svenska Kullagerfabriken – SKF.  
1934: Erich Franke invented the wire roller bearing based on the principle of embedded rolling elements.  
Over time, numerous further variants emerged. In particular, manufacturing accuracy and lubricant development advanced further. Numerous standards also established common standard dimensions, thus simplifying design and manufacturing. Today bearings with integrated sensors such as electronic force and wear measurement are offered.  

1883 Friedrich Fischer built the first ball grinding machine in Schweinfurt, thus laying the foundation for industrial production of sufficiently accurate round steel balls and the rolling bearing industry. In the same year he founded the company Kugelfischer. His employee Wilhelm Höpflinger significantly advanced the ball grinding machine.

en_bearing_mechanical#0.title: Bearing (mechanical)
en_bearing_mechanical#0.text:
A bearing is a machine element that constrains relative motion to only the desired motion and reduces friction between moving parts. The design of the bearing may, for example, provide for free linear movement of the moving part or for free rotation around a fixed axis; or, it may prevent a motion by controlling the vectors of normal forces that bear on the moving parts. Most bearings facilitate the desired motion by minimizing friction. Bearings are classified broadly according to the type of operation, the motions allowed, or the directions of the loads (forces) applied to the parts.
The term "bearing" is derived from the verb "to bear"; a bearing being a machine element that allows one part to bear (i.e., to support) another. The simplest bearings are bearing surfaces, cut or formed into a part, with varying degrees of control over the form, size, roughness, and location of the surface. Other bearings are separate devices installed into a machine or machine part. The most sophisticated bearings for the most demanding applications are very precise components; their manufacture requires some of the highest standards of current technology.

Rotary bearings hold rotating components such as shafts or axles within mechanical systems and transfer axial and radial loads from the source of the load to the structure supporting it. The simplest form of bearing, the plain bearing, consists of a shaft rotating in a hole. Lubrication is used to reduce friction. Lubricants come in different forms, including liquids, solids, and gases. The choice of lubricant depends on the specific application and factors such as temperature, load, and speed.

ko_bearing#1.text:
수송 기계부터 시작해서 각종 기계에 널리 사용되며, 회전하는 부분이 있는 기계장치에는 반드시 존재한다.
베어링의 종류는 회전운동용, 직선운동용으로 나눌수도 있고, 무한순환운동 방식과 유한순환 운동 방식으로 구분할 수도 있다.
각 운동방식에서의 구름체 종류나 주행축 형상에 따라 더 다양하게 구분할 수 있다.

나무 롤러 형태의 롤링 베어링의 발명은 아주 고대에 일어났으며 아마도 바퀴보다 먼저 발명되었을 것이다. 고대 이집트인들이 나무줄기 썰매에서 롤러 베어링을 사용했다는 것이 현대의 추측이다. 그들의 무덤에 평면 베어링으로 구성되어 있는 액체 윤활 주자와 썰매를 이용하여 돌을 이동한 그림을 그려놓았다. 또한 베어링이 핸드 드릴과 함께 사용하고 있는 그림도 존재한다.
레오나르도 다빈치는 약 1500년에 헬리콥터에 대한 그의 디자인에 볼 베어링을 통합시켰다. 이것은 항공 설계 베어링의 첫 번째 기록이다. 그러나 아고스티노 라멜리는 롤러 추력 베어링을 처음 스케치를 처음한 사람이다. 볼 및 롤러 베어링의 문제는 볼 또는 롤러가 둘러싸여 짐에 따라 예측 할 수 있는 서로가 원인이 되는 마찰력이 추가적으로 발생한다는 것이다.
캡쳐 또는 갇힌 볼 베어링은 원래 갈릴레오가 17세기에 고안했다.
ko_bearing#1.en:
Used from transportation machinery to various machines, rolling bearings are necessarily present in any mechanical device with rotating parts.  
Rolling bearings can be classified into rotating motion type and linear motion type, or into infinite cycle motion type and finite cycle motion type.  
They can be further distinguished according to the type of rolling element or the shape of the shaft in each motion mode.  

The invention of wooden roller-type rolling bearings dates back to an extremely ancient time and may have predated the invention of wheels. It is currently believed that ancient Egyptians used roller bearings in wooden sleds. Drawings found in their tombs depict a liquid-lubricated flat bearing system used to move stones with sleds. Additionally, drawings showing bearings used in hand drills also exist.  
Leonardo da Vinci integrated ball bearings into his helicopter design around 1500—this is considered the first recorded use of bearings in aviation design. However, Agostino Ramelli was the first person to sketch a roller thrust bearing. The problem with ball and roller bearings is that balls or rollers generate additional friction forces that are mutually causative and unpredictable under load.  
Caged or captured ball bearings were originally conceived by Galileo in the 17th century.

ko_ball_bearing#2.title: 볼 베어링
ko_ball_bearing#2.text:
접촉각이 클수록(일반적으로 10~45도 범위) 지지되는 축 하중은 높지만 반경 하중은 낮아진다. 터빈, 제트 엔진 및 치과 장비와 같은 고속 응용 분야에서는 볼에 의해 생성되는 원심력이 내륜 및 외륜의 접촉각을 변경한다. 질화 규소와 같은 세라믹은 낮은 밀도(강철의 40%) 때문에 이러한 응용 분야에서 정기적으로 사용된다. 이러한 재료는 원심력을 크게 줄이고 고온 환경에서도 잘 작동한다. 또한 유리나 도자기처럼 균열되거나 부서지지 않고 베어링 강과 유사한 방식으로 마모되는 경향이 있다. 대부분의 자전거는 헤드셋에 앵귤러 콘택트 베어링을 사용하는데, 이는 이러한 베어링에 가해지는 힘이 반경 방향과 축 방향 모두에 있기 때문이다.

축방향 또는 스러스트 볼 베어링은 나란히 놓인 레이스를 사용한다. 축방향 하중은 베어링을 통해 직접 전달되는 반면, 반경 방향 하중은 잘 지지되지 않고 레이스를 분리시키는 경향이 있어 더 큰 반경 방향 하중은 베어링을 손상시킬 가능성이 높다.

딥 그루브 레이디얼 베어링에서 레이스 치수는 그 안에 들어 있는 볼의 치수와 가깝다. 딥 그루브 베어링은 얕은 그루브보다 더 높은 하중을 지지한다.
ko_ball_bearing#2.en:
The larger the contact angle (typically in the range of 10~45 degrees), the higher the axial load supported, but the radial load decreases. In high-speed applications such as turbines, jet engines, and dental equipment, the centrifugal force generated by the balls alters the contact angles of the inner and outer rings. Ceramics such as silicon nitride, due to their low density (40% of steel), are used regularly in these applications. These materials significantly reduce centrifugal force and operate well in high-temperature environments. Additionally, they tend to wear like bearing steel, without cracking or shattering, similar to glass or ceramic. Most bicycles use angular contact bearings in the headset, because the forces applied to these bearings act in both radial and axial directions.

Thrust ball bearings use parallel races. Axial loads are directly transmitted through the bearing, while radial loads are poorly supported and tend to separate the races, making it more likely that higher radial loads will damage the bearing.

In deep groove radial bearings, the race dimensions are close to the ball size. Deep groove bearings support higher loads than shallow groove bearings.

ko_ball_bearing#19.title: 볼 베어링
ko_ball_bearing#19.text:
시계학에서 장 라살 회사는 무브먼트의 두께를 줄이기 위해 볼 베어링을 사용하는 시계 무브먼트를 설계했다. 0.20mm 볼을 사용하여 칼리버 1200은 두께가 1.2mm에 불과했으며, 이는 여전히 가장 얇은 기계식 시계 무브먼트이다.
항공우주 베어링은 상업용, 개인용 및 군용 항공기의 많은 응용 분야에서 사용되며, 여기에는 풀리, 기어박스 및 제트 엔진 샤프트가 포함된다. 재료에는 M50 공구강(AMS6491), 탄소 크롬강(AMS6444), 내식성 AMS5930, 440C 스테인리스강, 질화 규소(세라믹) 및 탄화 티타늄 코팅 440C가 포함된다.
스케이트보드 (장비) 바퀴에는 두 개의 베어링이 포함되어 있으며, 이들은 축 방향 및 반경 방향으로 시간에 따라 변하는 하중을 모두 받는다. 가장 일반적으로 베어링 608-2Z(보어 직경 8mm의 60 시리즈 딥 그루브 볼 베어링)가 사용된다.
초보자용부터 전문가용 또는 대회용 등 다양한 요요에는 볼 베어링이 통합되어 있다.
많은 피젯 스피너 장난감은 무게를 추가하고 장난감이 회전할 수 있도록 여러 개의 볼 베어링을 사용한다.
원심펌프에서.
철도 기관차 차축 저널. 철도가 디젤 엔진으로 전환되기 전 최신 고속 증기 기관차의 측면 로드 작동.

볼 크기는 주어진 내경 또는 외경(둘 다 아님)에 대해 시리즈가 증가함에 따라 증가한다.
ko_ball_bearing#19.en:
In horology, La Salle Company designed a watch movement using ball bearings to reduce the thickness of the movement. The Caliber 1200, using 0.20 mm balls, has a thickness of only 1.2 mm, which remains the thinnest mechanical watch movement to date.  
Aerospace bearings are used in numerous applications of commercial, personal, and military aircraft, including pulleys, gearboxes, and jet engine shafts. Materials include M50 tool steel (AMS6491), carbon chromium steel (AMS6444), corrosion-resistant AMS5930, 440C stainless steel, silicon nitride (ceramic), and titanium nitride-coated 440C.  
Skateboard (equipment) wheels contain two bearings that carry both axial and radial loads that vary with time. The most commonly used bearing is 608-2Z (a 60-series deep groove ball bearing with an 8 mm bore).  
Ball bearings are integrated into various levels, from beginner to expert or competition-grade.  
Many pinwheel toy devices use multiple ball bearings to add weight and allow the toy to rotate.  
In centrifugal pumps.  
Railway locomotive axle journals. Railways' side loading operation prior to the transition to diesel engines in the latest high-speed steam locomotives.  

Ball size increases as the series increases for a given inner or outer diameter (not both).

en_ball_bearing#8.title: Ball bearing
en_ball_bearing#8.text:
While ceramic hybrid bearings use ceramic balls in place of steel ones, they are constructed with steel inner and outer rings; hence the hybrid designation. While the ceramic material itself is stronger than steel, it is also stiffer, which results in increased stresses on the rings, and hence decreased load capacity. Ceramic balls are electrically insulating, which can prevent 'arcing' failures if current should be passed through the bearing. Ceramic balls can also be effective in environments where lubrication may not be available (such as in space applications). In some settings only a thin coating of ceramic is used over a metal ball bearing.
Fully ceramic bearings
These bearings make use of both ceramic balls and race. These bearings are impervious to corrosion and rarely require lubrication if at all. Due to the stiffness and hardness of the balls and race these bearings are noisy at high speeds. The stiffness of the ceramic makes these bearings brittle and liable to crack under load or impact. Because both ball and race are of similar hardness, wear can lead to chipping at high speeds of both the balls and the race, which can cause sparking.
Self-aligning
Self-aligning ball bearings, such as the Wingqvist bearing shown in the picture, are constructed with the inner ring and ball assembly contained within an outer ring that has a spherical raceway. This construction allows the bearing to tolerate a small angular misalignment resulting from shaft or housing deflections or improper mounting.

ko_lubrication#0.title: 윤활
ko_lubrication#0.text:
윤활(潤滑, lubrication)은 마찰이나 마모의 감쇄, 베어링의 냉각의 촉진, 이물(異物)의 배제 및 녹의 발생 방지 등을 위해 수행하는 행위이다.
구름베어링은 기본적으로 구름 마찰에 의하며 이는 윤활이 불필요할 뿐 아니라, 윤활제에 의해 점성 저항(粘性抵抗)이 생겨 오히려 구름 마찰을 크게 하는 결과가 된다. 그러나 실제로는 구름베어링의 궤도 면에서는 하중에 의해 구름베어링 접촉면 변형에 의한 차동(差動)미끄럼이 생기게 되며, 리테이너와 전동체(轉動體) 사이에서는 미끄럼 마찰이 생긴다. 그러므로 구름베어링에서도 윤활은 구름 성능 향상을 위해서 중요하다.
윤활유는 광유계(鑛油系)·동식물유계·합성유계 등 다수 있는데, 일반적으로는 광유계 윤활유가 많이 사용된다.
그리스는 반고체(半固體) 또는 고체상(狀)의 윤활제이며, 윤활유에 비하여 점도가 높지만 밀봉성(密封性)이 좋아서 자주 기름을 칠 필요가 없는 적용 개소에 사용된다.
그리스는 증주제(Thickner)의 종류에 따라 리튬(Li Grease), 칼슘(Ca Grease), 나트륨(Fibre Grease), 우레아계(Urea Grease) 등, 또 특성으로부터는 내수성(耐水性, Ca Grease) 및 내열성(Fibre Grease) 등으로 분류된다.
ko_lubrication#0.en:
Lubrication (lubrication) is a process performed to reduce friction and wear, enhance bearing cooling, exclude contaminants, and prevent corrosion.  
Rolling bearing operates essentially on rolling friction, which means lubrication is unnecessary, and in fact, the viscosity resistance generated by lubricants increases rolling friction. However, in reality, on the raceway surface of rolling bearings, differential sliding occurs due to deformation of the contact surface under load, and sliding friction occurs between the retainer and the rotating element. Therefore, lubrication is also important in rolling bearings to improve rolling performance.  
Lubricants are classified into several types such as mineral oil-based, animal and vegetable oil-based, and synthetic-based, with mineral oil-based lubricants being widely used.  
Grease is a semi-solid or solid lubricant with higher viscosity than liquid lubricants, but it has better sealing properties and is thus frequently used in applications where oil coating is unnecessary.  
Grease is classified according to the type of thickener into lithium (Li grease), calcium (Ca grease), sodium (Fibre grease), urea-based (Urea grease), and according to its properties into water-resistant (Ca grease) and heat-resistant (Fibre grease) types.

ko_ball_bearing#9.title: 볼 베어링
ko_ball_bearing#9.text:
세라믹 볼은 일반적으로 레이스보다 단단하다. 마모로 인해 시간이 지남에 따라 레이스에 홈이 생길 것이다. 이는 성능에 심각한 해를 끼칠 수 있는 평평한 지점을 남길 수 있는 볼의 마모보다 선호된다. 세라믹 하이브리드 베어링은 강철 볼 대신 세라믹 볼을 사용하지만, 강철 내륜과 외륜으로 구성된다. 따라서 하이브리드라는 명칭이 붙는다. 세라믹 재료 자체는 강철보다 강하지만, 더 단단하여 링에 가해지는 응력이 증가하고, 결과적으로 하중 용량이 감소한다. 세라믹 볼은 전기 절연성이 있어 전류가 베어링을 통과할 경우 '아크' 고장을 방지할 수 있다. 세라믹 볼은 윤활이 불가능한 환경(예: 우주 응용 분야)에서도 효과적일 수 있다. 일부 환경에서는 금속 볼 베어링 위에 얇은 세라믹 코팅만 사용된다.
완전 세라믹 베어링
이 베어링은 세라믹 볼과 레이스를 모두 사용한다. 이 베어링은 부식에 강하고 윤활이 거의 필요하지 않다. 볼과 레이스의 강성과 경도 때문에 이 베어링은 고속에서 소음이 발생한다. 세라믹의 강성 때문에 이 베어링은 취약하며 하중이나 충격으로 인해 균열이 발생하기 쉽다. 볼과 레이스 모두 비슷한 경도를 가지기 때문에 마모는 고속에서 볼과 레이스 모두에 파편을 유발할 수 있으며, 이는 스파크를 유발할 수 있다.
자동 조심 베어링
ko_ball_bearing#9.en:
Ceramic balls are generally harder than races. Due to wear, grooves will form in the races over time. This is preferred over ball wear, which can leave flat spots that severely affect performance. Ceramic hybrid bearings use ceramic balls instead of steel balls, but are composed of steel inner and outer rings. Therefore, the name "hybrid" is applied. Although ceramic materials themselves are stronger than steel, they are harder, which increases the stress on the rings, resulting in a reduced load capacity. Ceramic balls have excellent electrical insulation, preventing arc damage if current passes through the bearing. Ceramic balls can be effective in environments where lubrication is impossible (e.g., space applications). In some environments, only a thin ceramic coating is applied over metal ball bearings.

Fully ceramic bearings  
This bearing uses both ceramic balls and races. This bearing is corrosion-resistant and requires almost no lubrication. Due to the stiffness and hardness of both balls and races, this bearing generates noise at high speeds. Because of the strength of ceramic, this bearing is brittle and prone to cracking under load or impact. Since both balls and races have similar hardness, wear at high speeds can cause both to generate fragments, which may lead to sparking.

Automatic self-aligning bearings

en_ball_bearing#17.title: Ball bearing
en_ball_bearing#17.text:
In horology, the Jean Lassale company designed a watch movement that used ball bearings to reduce the thickness of the movement. Using 0.20 mm balls, the Calibre 1200 was only 1.2 mm thick, which still is the thinnest mechanical watch movement.
Aerospace bearings are used in many applications on commercial, private and military aircraft including pulleys, gearboxes and jet engine shafts. Materials include M50 tool steel (AMS6491), carbon chrome steel (AMS6444), the corrosion resistant AMS5930, 440C stainless steel, silicon nitride (ceramic) and titanium carbide-coated 440C.
A skateboard wheel contains two bearings, which are subject to both axial and radial time-varying loads. Most commonly bearing 608-2Z is used (a deep groove ball bearing from series 60 with 8 mm bore diameter)
Many yo-yos, ranging from beginner to professional or competition grade, incorporate ball bearings.
Many fidget spinner toys use multiple ball bearings to add weight, and to allow the toy to spin.
In centrifugal pumps.
Railroad locomotive axle journals. Side rod action of newest high speed steam locomotives before railroads were converted to diesel engines.

The ball size increases as the series increases, for any given inner diameter or outer diameter (not both). The larger the ball the greater the load carrying capacity. Series 200 and 300 are the most common.

en_bearing_mechanical#6.title: Bearing (mechanical)

en_plain_bearing#5.title: Plain bearing
en_plain_bearing#5.text:
Aluminum-backed Frelon are commonly used in corrosive environments because the Frelon is chemically inert.

A common plain bearing design utilizes a hardened and polished steel shaft and a softer bronze bushing. The bushing is replaced whenever it has worn too much.
Common bronze alloys used for bearings include: SAE 841, SAE 660 (CDA 932), SAE 863, and CDA 954.

A cast iron bearing can be used with a hardened steel shaft because the coefficient of friction is relatively low. The cast iron glazes over therefore wear becomes negligible.

In harsh environments, such as ovens and dryers, a copper and graphite alloy, commonly known by the trademarked name graphalloy, is used. The graphite is a dry lubricant, therefore it is low friction and low maintenance. The copper adds strength, durability, and provides heat dissipation characteristics.

Unalloyed graphite bearings are used in special applications, such as locations that are submerged in water.

Known as jewel bearings, these bearings use jewels, such as sapphire, ruby, and garnet. Jewel bearings are used in precision instruments where low friction, long life, and dimensional accuracy are important. Their main use is in mechanical watches.

Solid plastic plain bearings are now increasingly popular due to dry-running lubrication-free behavior. Solid polymer plain bearings are low weight, corrosion resistant, and maintenance free.

de_gleitlager#0.title: Gleitlager
de_gleitlager#0.text:
Das Gleitlager ist neben dem Wälzlager die im Maschinen- und Gerätebau am häufigsten gebrauchte Lagerbauart.
Gleitlager sind Maschinenelemente, die dazu dienen, die Reibung zwischen zwei sich gegeneinander bewegenden Oberflächen zu verringern. Häufig unterstützen und führen sie eine Welle oder Achse, die sich relativ zum Lagergehäuse dreht oder verschiebt.
Wirkprinzipien eines Gleitlagers:

Reibung: Zwischen zwei sich berührenden Oberflächen tritt Reibung auf. Gleitlager minimieren diese Reibung durch ihre Materialauswahl und Konstruktion.
Schmierung: Um die Reibung weiter zu reduzieren, können die Kontaktflächen durch Schmierstoffe getrennt werden. Diese Schmierstoffe können Flüssigkeiten (wie Öl oder Wasser), Gase oder feste Stoffe sein.

Man unterscheidet zwischen ungeschmierten bzw. selbstschmierenden Gleitlagern, hydrodynamischen Gleitlagern und hydrostatischen Gleitlagern.
In ungeschmierten oder selbstschmierenden Gleitlagern werden reibungsarme Werkstoffpaarungen verwendet. Mitunter hat einer der beiden Partner eine sogenannte „Selbstschmierungs-Eigenschaft“ (zum Beispiel ein mit Blei oder Zinn legierter Werkstoff, ein Kunststoff wie PTFE oder Technische Keramik). Der zweite Partner (bei Radiallagern in der Regel die Welle) ist meist aus Stahl.

Bei hydrodynamischen Gleitlagern „schwimmt“ die Welle auf dem Schmierfilm, was die Reibung auf ein Minimum reduziert. Beim Anlauf der Welle entsteht zunächst Mischreibung. Mit zunehmender Drehzahl wird der Schmierstoff durch die Bewegung der Welle in den Spalt zwischen Welle und Lagerbuchse gezogen.
de_gleitlager#0.en:
The sliding bearing is, together with the rolling bearing, the most commonly used bearing type in machinery and equipment construction.  
Sliding bearings are machine elements designed to reduce friction between two mutually moving surfaces. Frequently, they support and guide a shaft or axle that rotates or shifts relatively to the bearing housing.  
Working principles of a sliding bearing:  

Friction: Friction occurs between two contacting surfaces. Sliding bearings minimize this friction through their material selection and design.  
Lubrication: To further reduce friction, the contacting surfaces can be separated by lubricants. These lubricants can be liquids (such as oil or water), gases, or solids.  

Sliding bearings are distinguished between unlubricated or self-lubricating bearings, hydrodynamic bearings, and hydrostatic bearings.  
In unlubricated or self-lubricating bearings, friction-free material pairs are used. Occasionally, one of the two partners has a so-called "self-lubricating property" (for example, a material alloyed with lead or tin, a plastic such as PTFE or technical ceramics). The second partner (in radial bearings usually the shaft) is typically made of steel.  

In hydrodynamic sliding bearings, the shaft "floats" on the lubricant film, reducing friction to a minimum. At startup of the shaft, initial mixed friction occurs. As the rotational speed increases, the lubricant is drawn into the gap between the shaft and the bearing housing by the motion of the shaft.

de_waelzlager#8.title: Wälzlager
de_waelzlager#8.text:
SKF gibt zum Beispiel für einige Lager eine Lebensdauer von 2 Mrd. Umdrehungen an, was jedoch oft weit überschritten wird.
Ob ein Lager seine Lebensdauer erreicht, hängt stark von den Einsatzbedingungen ab. Hohe Lagerbelastungen sollten ebenso möglichst vermieden werden wie schmutzige Einsatzbedingungen, hohe Betriebstemperaturen oder Eindringen von Wasser ins Lager. Um das Eindringen von Schmutz und Wasser zu erschweren, gibt es viele Lager auch mit integrierter Dichtung. Andernfalls sollten sie in ein Lagergehäuse eingesetzt werden, das etwa mit einem Wellendichtring abgedichtet ist.
Defekte Lager erkennt man an

ungleichmäßigem, rauem Lauf beim Drehen mit der Hand,
Schwergängigkeit, die über die übliche Reibung der Dichtscheiben hinausgeht,
fühlbarem Lagerspiel oder
Laufgeräuschen und Vibrationen bei Betriebsdrehzahl oder
Wärmeentwicklung, im Extremfall Auftreten von Anlauffarben oder
erhöhtem Energiebedarf von Antriebsmotoren.
Zum Beispiel sind Schäden an Lagern im Auto oft durch ungewöhnliche Geräusche bemerkbar. Dazu zählen metallische Rollgeräusche, Pfeif- und Schleifgeräusche sowie mahlende Klänge bei gerader Fahrt. In Kurven können Klopf- oder Vibrationsgeräusche auftreten. Verändertes Fahrverhalten, wie ein instabiles Lenkgefühl oder einseitiges Ziehen beim Bremsen, deutet ebenfalls auf mögliche Defekte hin.
Gedichtete Wälzlager können vom Hersteller mit einer Lebensdauerschmierung angeboten werden. Ungeschmierte Lager fallen sogleich aus.
de_waelzlager#8.en:
SKF gives, for example, a life of 2 billion revolutions for some bearings, which however is often far exceeded.  
Whether a bearing reaches its life depends strongly on the operating conditions. High bearing loads should be avoided just as much as dirty operating conditions, high operating temperatures, or water ingress into the bearing. To make it harder for dirt and water to enter, many bearings are also provided with an integrated seal. Otherwise, they should be installed in a bearing housing that is sealed, for example, with a shaft seal.  
Defective bearings can be recognized by  

uneven, rough running when turned by hand,  
severe difficulty, exceeding the normal friction of the sealing rings,  
feelable bearing play or  
running noises and vibrations at operating speed or  
heat generation, in extreme cases appearance of running colors or  
increased power consumption of drive motors.  
For example, bearing damage in a car is often noticeable through unusual noises. This includes metallic rolling noises, whistling and rubbing noises, as well as grinding sounds during straight-line driving. In curves, knocking or vibration noises may occur. Altered driving behavior, such as an unstable steering feel or pulling on one side during braking, also indicates possible defects.  
Sealed rolling bearings can be offered by the manufacturer with a life-lubrication. Unlubricated bearings fail immediately.

en_tribology#17.title: Tribology
en_tribology#17.text:
Otherwise for a deformation that expands only in the inner circle there will be increasing friction coefficients.

To reduce friction between surfaces and keep wear under control, materials called lubricants are used. Unlike what you might think, these are not just oils or fats, but any fluid material that is characterized by viscosity, such as air and water. Of course, some lubricants are more suitable than others, depending on the type of use they are intended for: air and water, for example, are readily available, but the former can only be used under limited load and speed conditions, while the second can contribute to the wear of materials.
What we try to achieve by means of these materials is a perfect fluid lubrication, or a lubrication such that it is possible to avoid direct contact between the surfaces in question, inserting a lubricant film between them. To do this there are two possibilities, depending on the type of application, the costs to address and the level of "perfection" of the lubrication desired to be achieved, there is a choice between:

Fluidostatic lubrication (or hydrostatic in the case of mineral oils) – which consists in the insertion of lubricating material under pressure between the surfaces in contact;
Fluid fluid lubrication (or hydrodynamics) – which consists in exploiting the relative motion between the surfaces to make the lubricating material penetrate.

The viscosity is the equivalent of friction in fluids, it describes the ability of fluids to resist the forces that cause a change in shape.
Thanks to Newton's studies, a deeper understanding of the phenomenon has been achieved.

The raceways of a conical bearing are usually formed by an outer bearing shell and an inner cone. The bearing shell is inserted, pressed in, or screwed into a housing. The inner cone consists either of the raceway on a forged shaft or shaft, or it is assembled as a separate component screwed onto the shaft or shaft. The balls are nowadays often guided in a ball cage, which simplifies assembly. The ball raceways usually correspond only approximately to the shape of a cone (conical frustum). Conical bearings are usually installed in pairs and preloaded. The paired installation can be carried out in tandem, O-, or X-configuration. ko_ball_bearing#12.title: 볼 베어링
ko_ball_bearing#12.text:
또한 베어링이 회전하지 않는 경우, 베어링에 가해지는 진동력은 베어링 레이스 또는 구름 요소에 충격 손상을 일으킬 수 있으며, 이를 브리넬링이라고 한다. 베어링이 짧은 호를 따라 회전하고 윤활유를 구름 요소에서 멀리 밀어낼 때 발생하는 두 번째로 작은 형태는 가짜 브리넬링이라고 한다.
회전하는 베어링의 경우 동적 하중 용량은 베어링이 1,000,000 사이클을 견디는 하중을 나타낸다.
베어링이 회전하지만 한 바퀴보다 짧게 지속되는 심한 하중을 받는 경우, 베어링이 최대 하중 동안 회전하지 않으므로 계산에 정적 최대 하중을 사용해야 한다.
딥 그루브 레이디얼 베어링에 측면 토크가 가해지면 타원형의 고르지 않은 힘이 구름 요소에 의해 외륜에 가해지며, 외륜의 반대편 두 영역에 집중된다. 외륜이 충분히 강하지 않거나 지지 구조에 의해 충분히 지지되지 않으면 외륜은 측면 토크 응력으로 인해 타원형으로 변형되어 구름 요소가 빠져나갈 수 있을 만큼 간격이 커질 때까지 변형된다. 그러면 내륜이 튀어나와 베어링이 구조적으로 붕괴된다.
레이디얼 베어링에 가해지는 측면 토크는 구름 요소가 가장 높은 측면 토크 위치에서 모두 함께 미끄러지려는 시도 때문에 구름 요소를 같은 간격으로 유지하는 케이지에도 압력을 가한다.
ko_ball_bearing#12.en:
Additionally, when a bearing is not rotating, the vibrational force applied to the bearing may cause impact damage to the bearing race or rolling elements, a phenomenon known as brinelling. The second smallest form occurring when a bearing rotates over a short arc and pushes lubricant away from the rolling elements is called false brinelling.  
For a rotating bearing, the dynamic load capacity is defined as the load that the bearing can withstand for 1,000,000 cycles.  
When a bearing is subjected to severe loads for a duration shorter than one revolution, even though the bearing is rotating, it does not rotate during the maximum load period, thus a static maximum load must be used in the calculation.  
When a side torque is applied to a deep groove radial bearing, an uneven elliptical force is transmitted to the outer ring via the rolling elements, concentrating on two opposite areas of the outer ring. If the outer ring is not sufficiently strong or adequately supported by the support structure, the outer ring deforms elastically into an elliptical shape under side torque stress until the spacing between the rolling elements becomes large enough for them to disengage. At this point, the inner ring may pop out, leading to structural collapse of the bearing.  
The side torque applied to a radial bearing exerts pressure on the cage, which maintains the rolling elements at equal spacing, due to the attempt of all rolling elements to slide together at the position of maximum side torque.

2006: FAG Kugelfischer und INA werden in der Schaeffler KG zusammengefasst und dadurch zum zweitgrößten Wälzlagerkonzern der Welt; nach SKF, dessen weltweit größtes Werk sich ebenfalls in Deutschland (Schweinfurt) befindet.

Die umgangssprachlich bekannten Kugellager sind eine Untergruppe der Wälzlager, bei denen Kugeln als Wälzkörper dienen.
Bei modernen Wälzlagern werden die Wälzkörper (Kugeln, Zylinder, Nadeln, Tonnen oder Kegel) durch einen Käfig in gleichem Abstand gehalten. Ältere Wälzlagertypen und Sonderausführungen kommen ohne Käfig aus. Vor allem Wälzlager in Steuerungssystemen von Flugzeugen haben keinen Käfig. Dadurch können mehr Wälzkörper pro Lager eingesetzt werden, was die Belastbarkeit deutlich erhöht. Jedoch eignen sie sich nur bedingt für höhere Drehzahlen.
Käfigwerkstoff war früher wegen der erhöhten Laufruhe Messing. Heute wird der Käfig aus Kosten- und Gewichtsgründen oft aus (meist glasfaserverstärktem) Kunststoff (Polyamid) gefertigt. Bei vielen Wälzlagertypen wird ein Käfig aus niedriglegiertem, ungehärtetem Stahl verwendet. Messingkäfige gibt es weiterhin; insbesondere für größere Lager, bei denen sich die Werkzeugkosten für Kunststoff- oder Stahlblechkäfig nicht lohnen.

2006: FAG Ball bearings and INA are combined within Schaeffler KG and thus become the second largest rolling bearing company in the world; after SKF, whose largest plant is also located in Germany (Schweinfurt).

The commonly known ball bearings are a subgroup of rolling bearings, in which balls serve as rolling elements.  
In modern rolling bearings, the rolling elements (balls, cylinders, needles, cones or drums) are held at equal spacing by a cage. Older rolling bearing types and special designs operate without a cage. Especially rolling bearings in aircraft control systems do not have a cage. This allows for more rolling elements per bearing, significantly increasing load capacity. However, they are only marginally suitable for higher speeds.  
Cage materials were previously brass due to improved running smoothness. Today, cages are often manufactured from plastic (typically glass fiber-reinforced polyamide) for cost and weight reasons. In many rolling bearing types, a cage made of low-alloy, non-quenched steel is used. Brass cages are still available; particularly for larger bearings, where the tooling costs for plastic or steel sheet cages are not justified.

일반적으로 볼 베어링의 최대 하중은 베어링의 외경에 베어링의 폭(폭은 축 방향으로 측정됨)을 곱한 값에 비례한다.
베어링에는 정적 하중 정격이 있다. 이는 레이스웨이에서 특정 양의 소성 변형을 초과하지 않는 것을 기준으로 한다. 이 정격은 특정 응용 분야에서 크게 초과될 수 있다.

베어링이 제대로 작동하려면 윤활이 필요하다. 대부분의 경우 윤활제는 엘라스토하이드로다이내믹 효과(오일 또는 그리스에 의한)를 기반으로 하지만 극한 온도에서 작동하는 건식 윤활 베어링도 사용할 수 있다.

If the cage collapses or breaks, the rolling elements may gather together and cause the inner ring to lose its support and project out from the center.

Generally, the maximum load of a ball bearing is proportional to the product of the bearing outer diameter and the bearing width (width is measured in the axial direction).
Bearings have a static load rating. This is based on the condition that the raceway does not experience a specific amount of plastic deformation. This rating may be greatly exceeded in certain applications.

Bearings require lubrication to operate properly. In most cases, lubrication is based on elastohydrodynamic effects (oil or grease-based), but dry lubrication bearings that operate under extreme temperatures can also be used.
In order for a bearing to achieve its nominal life at the nominal maximum load, it must be lubricated with a lubricant (oil or grease) having a minimum dynamic viscosity (typically denoted by the Greek letter ν) that is equal to or greater than the recommended value.
The recommended dynamic viscosity is inversely proportional to the bearing diameter.
The recommended dynamic viscosity decreases with rotational speed. As a rough guideline: below 3000 RPM, a tenfold decrease in speed results in a sixfold increase in the recommended viscosity, and above 3000 RPM, a tenfold increase in speed results in a threefold decrease in the recommended viscosity.
The recommended dynamic viscosity for a bearing with an average of the bearing outer diameter and the shaft hole diameter of 50 mm rotating at 3000 RPM is 12 mm²/s.

en_bearing_mechanical#5.title: Bearing (mechanical)
en_bearing_mechanical#5.text:
Linear motion, e.g. drawer;
Spherical rotation, e.g. ball and socket joint;
Hinge motion, e.g. door, elbow, knee.

The first plain and rolling-element bearings were wood, closely followed by bronze. Over their history, bearings have been made of many materials, including ceramic, sapphire, glass, steel, bronze, and other metals. Plastic bearings made of nylon, polyoxymethylene, polytetrafluoroethylene, and UHMWPE, among other materials, are also in use today.

Watchmakers produce "jeweled" watches using sapphire plain bearings to reduce friction, thus allowing more precise timekeeping.
Even basic materials can have impressive durability. Wooden bearings, for instance, can still be seen today in old clocks or in water mills where the water provides cooling and lubrication.

By far, the most common bearing is the plain bearing, a bearing that uses surfaces in rubbing contact, often with a lubricant such as oil or graphite. A plain bearing may or may not be a discrete device. It may be nothing more than the bearing surface of a hole with a shaft passing through it, or of a planar surface that bears another (in these cases, not a discrete device); or it may be a layer of bearing metal either fused to the substrate (semi-discrete) or in the form of a separable sleeve (discrete). With suitable lubrication, plain bearings often give acceptable accuracy, life, and friction at minimal cost. Therefore, they are very widely used.
